'''Claire Kremen''' is an American conservation biologist. She is a professor of conservation biology at the [[University of British Columbia]], having formerly worked at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where she remains professor emerita.

==Early life and education==
Kremen graduated from [[Stanford University]] with a B.S. in Biology in 1982, and from [[Duke University]] with a PhD in Zoology in 1987.<ref>{{cite web |title=Claire Kremen |url=https://www.zoology.ubc.ca/person/claire-kremen |website=zoology.ubc.ca |accessdate=November 15, 2020}}</ref>

==Career==
Upon completing her PhD, Kremen spent 10 years working for nonprofit organizations in conservation biology.<ref name = "Dinolfo">{{cite web |last1=Dinolfo |first1=Adrianna |title=Interview: Claire Kremen, conservation biologist |url=https://www.dailycal.org/2015/04/24/interview-claire-kremen-conservation-biologist/ |website=dailycal.org |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=April 24, 2015}}</ref> She studied the impacts of [[Deforestation in Madagascar]], on species distributions with a Web-based biodiversity database.<ref name = "MacArthur">{{cite web |last1=Yang |first1=Sarah |title=Claire Kremen, UC Berkeley conservation biologist, wins MacArthur 'genius' fellowship |url=https://www.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/2007/09/24_kremen.shtml |website=berkeley.edu |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=September 24, 2007}}</ref> Kremen eventually returned to North American and accepted a faculty position at [[Princeton University]] for four years before becoming a professor of environmental science, policy and management at [[University of California, Berkeley]] (UC Berkeley).<ref name = "Dinolfo"/>

During her early tenure at UC Berkeley, Kremen also served as a member on the Committee on Status of Pollinators where she led the first global study on crop production that is reliant upon animal pollination.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Yang |first1=Sarah |title=Pollinators help one-third of world's crop production, says new study |url=https://www.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/2006/10/25_pollinator.shtml |website=berkeley.edu |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=October 25, 2006}}</ref> In recognition of her research, she was named a 2007 [[MacArthur Fellows Program]], which came with an unrestricted $500,000 award for the next five years.<ref name = "MacArthur"/> In the same year, Kremen was also awarded a Hellman Fellowship from the [[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]] for her project "How does Biological Diversity Promote Ecosystem Services: a Mechanistic Study of Almond Crop Pollination in a Changing California Landscape."<ref>{{cite web |title=Claire Kremen |url=http://www.hellmanfellows.org/fellows/claire-kremen/ |website=hellmanfellows.org |accessdate=November 15, 2020}}</ref> As an [[associate professor]] of environmental science, policy and management, Kremen led a study in 2011 which concluded that farmers could become more cost-efficient if they relied less on renting honey bees.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tam |first1=Jonathan |title=Study encourages farmers to rely less on rented bees |url=https://www.dailycal.org/2011/06/21/wild-bees-valued-up-to-2-4-billion-for-california-agriculture/ |website=dailycal.org |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=June 22, 2011}}</ref> In recognition of her academic achievements, Kremen was elected a Fellow of the California Academy of Sciences in 2013<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tuan |first1=Lydia |title=4 UC Berkeley faculty members elected fellows at the California Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.dailycal.org/2013/10/15/four-uc-berkeley-researchers-elected-fellows-at-the-california-academy-of-sciences/ |website=dailycal.org |accessdate=November 14, 2020 |date=October 15, 2013}}</ref> and appointed Editor in Chief of the journal ''Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems.''<ref>{{cite web |title=Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems welcomes new Field Chief Editor |url=https://blog.frontiersin.org/2018/03/12/frontiers-in-sustainable-food-systems-new-field-chief-editor/ |website=frontiersin.org |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=March 12, 2018}}</ref>

In 2019, Kremen left UC Berkeley to become one of the first [[University of British Columbia]] (UBC) President’s Excellence Chair in Biodiversity Studies at the UBC Institute for Resources, Environment and Sustainability.<ref>{{cite web |title=UBC IRES Welcomes Dr. Claire Kremen! |url=http://ires.ubc.ca/ubc-ires-welcomes-dr-claire-kremen/ |website=ires.ubc.ca |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=2019}}</ref> While serving in this role, she was awarded an honorary degree from the [[American Museum of Natural History]] in "recognition of her extraordinary contributions to science, education and society."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Balma |first1=Chris |title=UBC ecologist honored by American Museum of Natural History |url=https://science.ubc.ca/news/ubc-ecologist-honored-american-museum-natural-history |website=science.ubc.ca |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=September 26, 2019}}</ref> In 2020, Kremen was the recipient of the [[Volvo Environment Prize]] for "exploring the way to a sustainable world."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fawcett-Atkinson |first1=Marc |title=Pollinators key to sustainability, says Claire Kremen, 2020 Volvo |work=Yorkton This Week |url=https://www.yorktonthisweek.com/regional-news/pollinators-key-to-sustainability-says-claire-kremen-2020-volvo-environment-prize-winner-1.24239349 |accessdate=November 15, 2020 |date=November 15, 2020}}</ref>
